intent: B1 second-round remediation: 3.9 stat kwarg crash fix + F3 tests that actually reach the remediated branch
notes: **F1 (HIGH — Python 3.9 crash in `_is_reparse_point`)** — `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.9"`. The pre-fix helper called `entry_or_path.stat(follow_symlinks=False)` on ANY object with a `stat` attribute — including plain `pathlib.Path` objects, which arrive from `_contained_repo_path`'s per-component walk. `pathlib.Path.stat(follow_symlinks=)` is 3.10+; on 3.9 that call raises `TypeError` (not caught by the surrounding `except OSError`), which would crash every live `/files`, `/file`, `/raw` request. Fix: gate the DirEntry-native fast path behind `isinstance(entry_or_path, os.DirEntry)`, and route Path/str inputs through `os.stat(os.fspath(x), follow_symlinks=False)` (3.3+ API). Two new pins in `test_content_transport_slice3.py`: `test_reparse_check_uses_python_3_9_compatible_stat` (source-grep — asserts the isinstance gate exists), `test_reparse_check_uses_os_stat_for_path_inputs` (functional — records `os.stat` calls during `_is_reparse_point(Path)` and asserts the 3.3+ shape was used).

**F2 (MEDIUM — F3 tests did not reach the remediated exception branch)** — The prior `test_file_concurrently_removed_returns_404` and `test_raw_concurrently_removed_returns_404` pins deleted the file BEFORE the HTTP request, so `_contained_repo_path.resolve(strict=True)` returned None and the handler emitted 404 via the `target is None` check rather than the `except (FileNotFoundError, PermissionError)` branch inside `_handle_file`/`_handle_raw`. Codex proved this by observation: removing the specific `except` clause would leave the tests passing. Remediation:

Renamed the misleading pins to `test_file_missing_target_returns_404_via_containment` and `test_raw_missing_target_returns_404_via_containment`. Still valuable — they cover the containment-resolve 404 path — but no longer claim to exercise the read-time exception branch.

Added `test_file_unreadable_target_returns_404_on_posix` and `test_raw_unreadable_target_returns_404_on_posix` (POSIX-only via `pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32")`). Each seeds a file, `os.chmod(str(path), 0)`, then GETs the endpoint. Containment resolve and `is_file()` both succeed on the readable-parent + present-target state; `read_bytes()` raises `PermissionError`, which now reaches the remediated branch and returns 404. Cleanup in `finally` via `os.chmod(..., 0o644)`.

Added `test_read_exception_clause_names_both_error_classes` — source-grep on `gator-dashboard.py` locating `def _handle_file` and `def _handle_raw` bodies and asserting each contains `except (FileNotFoundError, PermissionError)` BEFORE `except OSError`. The ordering is load-bearing: `PermissionError` is an `OSError` subclass, so a bare `OSError` clause above the specific one would silently swallow the 404 taxonomy. Static guard that catches removal of either exception class from the clause.

Charter update in `scripts-dashboard.md::do_GET`: rewrote the "Error-taxonomy TRIPWIRE" text to name the correct pin set (source-grep + POSIX-branch + containment-path) and to document the ordering-matters property; added a new "Python 3.9 compat TRIPWIRE for `_is_reparse_point`" documenting the 3.10+ kwarg crash class and the isinstance-gated fix. Both TRIPWIREs cite the executable pins.

Test results: `tests/test_dashboard_ui/` 142 pass + 11 skipped on Windows (Python 3.13). +3 net vs. prior state (rename +0, added POSIX unreadable-target ×2, source-grep ×1, functional os.stat ×1 = +4; renamed pins ×0). POSIX-only pins (8 skipped locally, exercised on Ubuntu CI) include the two new chmod-permission tests. No regressions in Slice 1 (70/70) or Slice 2 (46/46).
The 3.9 crash is now catchable by CI without an explicit 3.9 matrix run — the source-grep + `os.stat`-call-recording pins fail on ANY Python version if the fix regresses.
